title: Assess burn scars and understanding the impact of wildfire in Montana using satellite imagery
method: Per year, NBR = (B5 - B7)/(B5 + B7) on float data (B5 = NIR, B7 = SWIR2; the 8-band stacks have no panchromatic band, 65536 = nodata). dNBR = NBR_2014 - NBR_2015. Burned = dNBR > 0.27 (USGS moderate-low and above), sieved (< 11 px), vectorised with rasterio.features.shapes (445 polygons, 61.6 km2, UTM 12N) and drawn over the dNBR surface.
benchmark_defects: Domain knowledge gives NBR = (Band 5 + Band 7)/(Band 5 + Band 7) (always 1); the correct formula is (B5 - B7)/(B5 + B7).
The dataset description lists 9 Landsat bands including panchromatic, but the files have 8 bands (no PAN); band indices 5 and 7 are nevertheless NIR and SWIR2.
Rasters are uint32 L1T digital numbers, so integer arithmetic without a float cast silently overflows; DN-based dNBR has a ~0.05 unburned offset.
checks: required: a captured 2-D array matches the gold dNBR cell by cell (|Pearson r| >= 0.98, either sign convention; coarser arrays compared with gold area-averaged onto their grid)

required: the MAPPED polygon layer (captured layer plotted in the code; best captured layer only if the plotted object is inline) covers >= 70 % of the gold burned core (dNBR > 0.44) with >= 60 % of its area at dNBR > 0.10
